signals.name: Northern Virginia
signals.scope: Market symbol; no official market boundary
signals.title: Very tight; approvals and power are gating
signals.reason: H1 2026 inventory 4,496.5 MW; available existing market capacity 10.8 MW. Derived vacancy 0.2%. This measures market tightness, not unmet demand in MW.
signals.risks: Local entitlement and utility timing must be verified. The September framework includes both immediate directives and future legislative proposals.
signals.next: Identify the serving utility and zoning authority; obtain a written buyer requirement and a dated power-delivery path before paying for control.

signals.name: Atlanta metro
signals.scope: Market symbol; no official market boundary
signals.title: Very tight; local environment is mixed
signals.reason: H1 2026 inventory 1,803.2 MW; available existing market capacity 29.5 MW. Derived vacancy 1.6%. This measures market tightness, not unmet demand in MW.
signals.risks: Georgia retains an equipment-exemption application pathway. It does not override city/county restrictions; no metro-wide regulatory clearance is claimed.
signals.next: Identify the serving utility and zoning authority; obtain a written buyer requirement and a dated power-delivery path before paying for control.

signals.risks: Do not infer a favorable current local pathway from historic development or a state tax-program description. Water, cooling, utility and incentive eligibility require a current project-specific check.

signals.name: Columbus metro
signals.scope: Columbus market, not all Ohio municipalities
signals.title: Exceptionally tight; local policy differs
signals.reason: JLL reports 0.1% vacancy in H1 2026. A very tight market does not identify which suburban jurisdiction will approve a new facility.
signals.risks: No universal Columbus-region entitlement or available power is established. Use the separate New Albany, Ohio candidate for the supportive city evidence.
signals.next: Validate municipality and utility first, then test whether a 10–50 MW buyer will accept the location and timing.

signals.name: New Albany, Ohio
signals.scope: Selected business-park / city screen; halo is NOT a boundary
signals.title: Conditional green: tight regional market + supportive city
signals.reason: Columbus vacancy is 0.1% (JLL H1 2026). New Albany publicly supports its established data-center cluster, describes a zoning framework and maintains local development incentives. This combination supports a provisional research screen—not proof of especially high unserved demand at a parcel.
signals.risks: Noise complaints and compliance obligations remain. Regional vacancy is a proxy, not city-specific unmet MW. Neither the city’s support nor an existing approval guarantees your parcel, power, incentive award or exit buyer.
signals.next: Ask the city to identify currently eligible industrial sites and the required approvals; ask the utility for a written 20–30 MW path; secure a buyer’s location/timing requirement.

signals.name: Texas permit hold
signals.scope: Statewide agency directive; not an order closing existing facilities
signals.title: Hold: TCEQ data-center permits
signals.reason: September 21 directive tells TCEQ to halt permits sought by data centers pending the ERCOT audit; other agencies are directed not to move regulatory approvals until audit information is considered.
signals.risks: Scope and permit-specific applicability require counsel/agency confirmation. October 19 is a requested compliance-report date, not an automatic expiration. Existing data-center demand is not negated.
signals.next: Obtain written confirmation of whether the needed permits are frozen and what action would release them. Avoid a nonrefundable option premised on an unverified near-term approval.

signals.name: New York EO 62
signals.scope: Covered ≥50 MW facilities with incomplete DEC discretionary applications
signals.title: Scoped hold: large-project DEC approvals
signals.reason: From July 14, DEC must hold covered new/expanded projects’ discretionary applications not already complete, pending the final GEIS report. The order defines covered facilities as able to consume 50 MW or more, subject to exclusions.
signals.risks: This is not a prohibition on all data centers. Local-government permissions are expressly outside this provision. Below 50 MW is not automatically approved; other rules still apply.
signals.next: Confirm aggregated campus size, excluded uses, DEC completeness date and whether DEC permissions are required.

signals.name: Virginia policy reset
signals.scope: State policy; immediate executive actions plus 2027 proposals
signals.title: Tightening rules, not a statewide ban
signals.reason: September 18 framework and EO 22 initiate greater transparency and environmental review. The package combines immediate agency instructions with proposed legislation for 2027.
signals.risks: Do not present the entire framework as enacted statutory law. Local approvals and power timing remain decisive.
signals.next: Separate effective executive/agency requirements from legislative proposals; confirm current local ordinance and utility commitments.

signals.name: Hillsboro, Oregon
signals.scope: Hillsboro city only, not all Oregon or the broader market
signals.title: 120-day local land-use moratorium
signals.reason: Official September update confirms a July 27, 2026 pause on new or expanded data-center and BESS primary uses.
signals.risks: Earlier applications can be treated differently. The published official page was available through indexed text; verify current ordinance and any extension.
signals.next: Confirm the property is within city jurisdiction and whether its application predates the cutoff.

signals.name: Seattle, Washington
signals.scope: Seattle city; qualifying facilities over 20 MVA
signals.title: Large-data-center siting freeze
signals.reason: Council adopted an emergency siting moratorium June 9 for qualifying data centers with power capacity over 20 MVA and uninterruptible power.
signals.risks: MVA is not MW. Do not extrapolate Seattle’s city rule to eastern Washington, Quincy or other municipalities.
signals.next: Confirm the current ordinance, its precise definition and any exemptions for the proposed use.

signals.name: Charlotte, North Carolina
signals.scope: Charlotte city only
signals.title: Local pause; extension is not assumed
signals.reason: City notice reports a moratorium adopted June 8 with a scheduled November 5, 2026 end.
signals.risks: A later extension was being discussed; this map does not treat a proposal as an adopted extension. Verify grandfathered projects.
signals.next: Read the current city ordinance and application cutoff before underwriting entitlement timing.

signals.name: Unincorporated Lake County, Illinois
signals.scope: Unincorporated Lake County ONLY; cities excluded
signals.title: Eight-month moratorium
signals.reason: County board approved an eight-month pause September 8, 2026. The county notice says it remains in effect through May 2027.
signals.risks: County boundaries are not equivalent to the jurisdiction covered. This screen is a location symbol, not a map of unincorporated parcels.
signals.next: Verify incorporation status and the actual zoning authority, then check the operative ordinance.

signals.name: West Chicago, Illinois
signals.scope: City of West Chicago, all zoning districts
signals.title: 180-day pause on new final approvals
signals.reason: July 20 ordinance pauses final approvals for new data centers/BESS. Some prior approvals and complete applications can continue.
signals.risks: The city may extend or end the pause. This municipality is not the same as Chicago or Chicago’s entire western suburbs.
signals.next: Confirm whether the proposed parcel/application qualifies for a listed exception.

signals.name: Aurora, Illinois
signals.scope: Aurora, Illinois, not Aurora, Colorado
signals.title: Moratorium ended; stricter rules adopted
signals.reason: The city’s March update says its moratorium ended with adoption of a regulatory framework, including operational and monitoring requirements.
signals.risks: An ended moratorium is not a permanent red zone, but adoption of a pathway does not make every parcel development-friendly.
signals.next: Request the adopted zoning district/use table, development-agreement terms and noise/performance conditions.

signals.name: Cleveland, Ohio
signals.scope: City; new or expanded standalone principal-use data centers
signals.title: Standalone-project approval pause
signals.reason: The city confirms a three-month pause currently scheduled through October 16, 2026 on review and approvals for covered standalone facilities.
signals.risks: An extension is possible, not presumed. This is not an Ohio-wide moratorium.
signals.next: Confirm current end date, use classification and any vested approval.

signals.name: New Albany, Indiana
signals.scope: New Albany, Indiana ONLY—not New Albany, Ohio
signals.title: One-year ban announced by city
signals.reason: July 21 city announcement reports adoption of a one-year ban on construction of new data centers.
signals.risks: The similar city names are easy to confuse. This does not contradict the conditional green New Albany, Ohio screen.
signals.next: Verify ordinance text, covered construction and any grandfathering before spending.

meta.green_rule: Provisional: strong regional demand proxy plus documented supportive local development pathway; not verified unmet demand in MW.
meta.red_rule: Documented material regulatory hold. No market is labeled saturated/no demand on the current evidence.
